title: I'd like to use iphone a bit, can you rush for me ?

messages.text: I'd like to use iphone a bit, can you rush for me ?

Yes: the iPhone is yours in about 3 min (around 08:51Z). The last robot test run is finishing now, and I stopped everything after it.
- Reserved for you: I queued a 20-min phone hold in your name, so no agent can touch the phone while you use it.
- Heat setting: the Xcode heat setting (Serious) may still be on, so the phone can feel slower than usual. That's expected.
- Results: all counted test runs for fix A were already done, so this stop costs nothing.
What you need to do: use the phone after about 08:51Z, and reply "done" here when you finish, so the tests can go on.

The iPhone is yours now (since 08:49Z), 2 min earlier than I said. The robot test ended and Safari is closed.
- Your hold: 20 min, until about 09:09Z. I'll extend it if you still need the phone then.
- No agent can use the phone while you hold it.
What you need to do: use the phone, then reply "done" here.

Thanks: I released your phone hold, so the agents can use the iPhone again.
- Next on the phone: nothing right now. Fix A's results are read without it, and fix B's follow-up needs Mac timing first.
What you need to do: nothing.

The Mac still sees no USB device at all after your re-plug, so the iPhone tests are stopped; can you tell me what you see?
- On the phone: does it show it is charging (the lightning bolt on the battery)?
- On the Mac: does Finder's sidebar list the iPhone under Locations?
- If it charges but Finder doesn't list it: the cable may be charge-only or the port may be bad; please try another cable.
- If neither works: restart the iPhone, then turn the Xcode heat setting back on as before.
- Nothing is lost: no counted run was cut; the test resumes once the phone is back.
What you need to do: reply with what you see (charging yes/no, Finder yes/no).
try to check again, i plug in the same type-c input
i was change the type-c input during i re-plug

Checked again at 10:11Z: the Mac's USB ports show no device at all, so the iPhone's cable is still not carrying data to this Mac.
- What the Mac sees: 3 USB buses, all empty; the iPhone tools list no phone.
- So it's the cable or the port, not the phone's settings: Trust and unlocking only matter once a device appears.
- Most likely: a charge-only cable, or a hub, dock or display in between.
What you need to do: try a different cable (ideally Apple's) straight into the Mac, then tell me if the phone shows it is charging and whether Finder lists it.

It works now: since 10:12Z the Mac sees the iPhone over the cable again, on the other Type-C port.
- So the first port was the problem, not the phone or the cable.
- The phone test restarts now; keep the cable on this port.
What you need to do: nothing; please keep off the phone while the test runs (about 1.5 h).
